author: simulation_agent

numbers.name: bead_diameter
numbers.note: the SI anchor: the particle in the bottle. An active particle of this size is a model choice, not a claim that these beads self-propel; the anchor exists because cards are authoritative in physical units (D7) and the store holds this diameter at E2

numbers.name: translational_diffusivity
numbers.note: D_T, the thermal translational diffusivity of the anchor sphere. Same relation as sim-20260917-001 and kb:tracer_diffusivity_expected

numbers.name: rotational_diffusivity
numbers.note: D_R, THERMALLY TIED to D_T through the sphere's rotational drag -- 3*D_T/bead_diameter**2. The person did not rule on the tie and this is the assumption a_thermal_rotation; the store holds nothing on rotational diffusivity (gap rotational_diffusivity_absent). In 2D the persistence time is 1/D_R, about a hundred seconds at this anchor

numbers.name: persistence_time_expected
numbers.note: the 2D relation tau_p = 1/D_R, the person's dimension. It is the input-side expectation the registered persistence_time estimator is read against, and not a result

numbers.name: temperature
numbers.note: a parameter of the noise amplitude, realised exactly by the model; the room's reading is why this value was chosen

numbers.name: peclet
numbers.note: held across arms; the centre of 041's Pe decades

numbers.name: diffusive_time
numbers.note: kb:tau_d's relation, d**2/D, applied to this card's inputs. NOT carried under the symbol tau_d: check 36 compares a symbol's formula text across cards and the store spells the input `diffusivity`, while this goal names the same quantity translational_diffusivity to keep it apart from the rotational one. Same relation, different formal-parameter name, so the symbol is left off rather than a second spelling registered. For an active particle it is the LONGEST of the candidate times, not the one that binds

numbers.name: self_propulsion_speed_max
numbers.note: v0 at the top of the Peclet range, from Pe = v0/(d*D_R), the steric convention (peclet_number_steric). The fastest particle sets the shortest active time

numbers.name: active_step_time
numbers.note: the time to self-propel one diameter; a step longer than a fraction of it moves a particle through a neighbour

numbers.name: shortest_resolved_time
numbers.note: the smallest of active_step_time (10 s), persistence_time_expected (100 s), diffusive_time (300 s). The formula grammar has no min(), so the comparison is made here and the formula names the winner

numbers.name: dt_resolution_factor
numbers.note: how far below the shortest resolved time the step must sit: two decades

numbers.name: integration_timestep_max
numbers.note: upper bound only; nothing in A1 bounds the step from below

assumptions.statement: D_R is tied to D_T by the sphere's rotational drag, D_R = 3 D_T / d^2, because the person fixed the anchor and not D_R separately, and a thermal sphere is the one relation that introduces no free number.
assumptions.falsifier: the person rules D_R an independent axis, or the store gains an entry for the anchor's rotational diffusivity that disagrees by more than a decade

assumptions.statement: One point in the middle of 041's grid, so the two questions share a condition and 041 can cite this result as its finite-size premise.
assumptions.falsifier: 041's S4 chooses a different centre, or a store entry places this point inside the clustered regime, where the box question has a different answer

assumptions.statement: Two decades below the shortest resolved time is the usual margin for an overdamped integrator; it is a convention and no convergence scan on this model has been run.
assumptions.falsifier: a timestep scan on this configuration showing the effective diffusivity flat over a wider range of steps replaces this factor with a measured one

kb_refs.claim: The laboratory's ambient temperature is 20 degrees Celsius, read off a thermometer by the operator. It is a reading and not a setpoint, and it is the room's rather than the sample's -- which is what makes it an operator reading at E3 and not a calibration at E2.
The diffusive time is the time a sphere needs to diffuse its own diameter, and it sets the shortest record length from which a mean squared displacement can be read.
The particles in the bottle in use have a diameter of 5 micrometres, with a coefficient of variation no greater than 2 per cent, measured directly by the operator on 2026-09-19.

note: The binding time is active_step_time, not the diffusive time bd_overdamped uses. For the free active configuration there is no contact time, so activity alone binds. S4 picks the step inside the interval (4.5.2).
